![A task board with a column for each status, including Ready and In QA](/lp/guide/en/blog-status-board.webp)

Your board says six tasks are in progress. In truth two are being written, three are waiting for review and one is in testing. You know because you asked. Anyone else looking at the board does not.

## Why it is hard

A handful of general statuses cannot hold a team's real process, so people add the missing part somewhere else: a note in the title, a tag, a message in chat. Then the board is no longer where you look to see what is going on, and the status meeting turns into going round the table.

## How Genos helps

A project can name its own **statuses**. Set them up and you get the built-in ones, including **Ready**, which means checked and ready to start. Then add your own, such as In QA or Waiting for client, and give each a colour.

```flow
Set up statuses
Add your own steps
Say what each counts as
Show a column for each
```

Every status **counts as** Open, WIP, Blocked, Pending, Closed or Rejected. That is what keeps the rest of the project honest. "In QA" counted as WIP is still not done, so progress, overdue and filters treat it that way.

Turn on **Show a column for each status** and the board gets one column per step, for everyone in the project. Drag a card into a column and it takes that status. The table's **Status** filter lists your names, and you can save the filter for the whole project.

## What you get

- **The answer on screen.** What is waiting for review is a column, not a question.
- **Your words.** People see the names your team already says out loud.
- **Numbers that still mean something.** A new step does not count as finished by accident.
- **One setup per project.** A design project and a support project can work differently.

Statuses belong to a project, and its owner or an editor sets them up. Milestones in that project use them too. Choose what a status counts as when you add it; you can change it only while no task, milestone or rule uses that status. A built-in status's is fixed.

## How to start

1. In the project, open the "…" menu and choose **Statuses and automation**.
2. Choose **Set up statuses**, then add the one or two steps your team talks about but cannot see.
3. Turn on **Show a column for each status** when the list looks right.

Keep it short. A column nobody moves a card into is a column to delete.
